stories.title: UCLA launches first digital humanities department to address AI and emerging technologies
stories.simple_summary: UCLA opened a new school department focused on teaching students about artificial intelligence and how it's changing society. They want to help people understand AI from the human perspective, not just the technical side.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have young family members interested in tech or education careers, this is a good program to know about — otherwise, it's mainly news for students and educators.

stories.title: Pope’s artificial intelligence guru admits he doesn’t use AI
stories.simple_summary: The Pope's AI expert admitted in an interview that he doesn't actually use AI tools himself. This is somewhat ironic since his job is to give advice about AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect your daily life — it's mostly a funny story about what experts do versus what they preach.

stories.title: Rogue AI agents hack government website, world leaders on edge of regulatory action
stories.simple_summary: Note: Headline 2 appears to be misleading clickbait lacking credible details. Treat with caution until verified by major news sources.
stories.why_it_matters: Be careful believing dramatic AI security stories without specifics — always check if major established news outlets are reporting the same story.

stories.title: Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar gives Google’s AI a face
stories.simple_summary: Google added a new feature where you can talk to their AI while watching a cartoon face on your screen that moves its lips and makes expressions. Right now, only big business customers can use it.
stories.why_it_matters: This is Google making their AI feel more like talking to a person — interesting but not something that affects most people yet.

stories.title: Bring your co-founder, partner, or colleague and get 50% off a second TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass
stories.simple_summary: This is an advertisement for a tech conference that's selling group discounts on tickets.
stories.why_it_matters: This is purely a sales promotion and doesn't involve any actual AI news — skip it.

stories.title: PrismML brings its tiny LLMs to Qualcomm-powered smart glasses
stories.simple_summary: A company called PrismML is putting tiny AI programs onto smart glasses made by Qualcomm. The goal is to make glasses smarter without needing them to connect to the internet constantly.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually make smart glasses actually useful for regular people instead of just expensive toys — but it's still in very early stages.

stories.title: Oracle sends force majeure notice on its New Mexico Stargate data center
stories.simple_summary: Oracle, a big tech company, just warned they might be late finishing a massive computer facility (data center) in New Mexico that won't be ready until 2028. This is important for their business contracts.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and large companies that depend on Oracle — nothing you need to act on as a small business owner.

stories.title: Jensen Huang talks about AI and climate change like a supervillain
stories.simple_summary: The CEO of Nvidia (a huge AI company) said that AI will help fight climate change, but getting there will be very difficult and cause disruption first. He sounded dramatic about it.
stories.why_it_matters: This is one executive's opinion about how AI might help the environment in the future — interesting to think about, but not something affecting you today.

stories.title: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone
stories.simple_summary: Meta (Facebook's parent company) is making tools so regular people can create simple video games using AI on their phones or web browser, without knowing how to code. The games would go on Meta's gaming platform.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're interested in making games as a hobby or small business, this could be a way to do it without learning programming — but it's only for Meta's platform.

stories.title: Meta’s Muse Charm looks like a Tamagotchi, but it’s tapping into a much newer trend
stories.simple_summary: Meta created a small AI gadget shaped like a charm you hang on a bag or keychain (like the retro Tamagotchi toy). It looks cute but contains AI inside.
stories.why_it_matters: This is Meta selling a new toy gadget — interesting as a tech trend but not essential for most people.

stories.title: Muse will apparently let you download its entire filesystem
stories.simple_summary: Two developers discovered that Meta's new Muse gadget can be tricked into giving them access to all of its internal files, including secret instruction files and system information. This is a security problem.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're considering buying Muse or similar products, this shows the company may have security weaknesses — wait to see if Meta fixes this problem first.

stories.title: Muse sure looks a lot like OpenClaw
stories.simple_summary: Meta's Muse AI gadget became very popular right after launch (topped the App Store charts) and has hundreds of thousands of daily users. Similar AI agent products are also becoming trendy.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI gadgets are becoming popular consumer products — it's mostly interesting news about tech trends, but doesn't require action on your part.
